assessment.title: Strings — Section-End Assessment
assessment.description: 12 MCQs. Passing threshold 70% is required alongside 8/10 problems completed to complete the available roadmap.

questions.text: Are "anagram" and "nagaram" anagrams of each other?
options: Only if they have the same prefix
questions.explanation: Both contain the same letters with the same multiplicities.
Defanging replaces each '.' with the bracketed literal '[.]'.

questions.text: With jewels = "aA" and stones = "aAAbbbb", how many stones are jewels?
questions.explanation: One 'a' and two 'A's match the jewel set, totalling 3.

questions.text: Can the ransom note "aab" be constructed from the magazine "aabbc"?
questions.explanation: The magazine has at least two 'a's and one 'b', which are exactly the required counts.

questions.text: For haystack = "sadbutsad" and needle = "sad", the index of the first occurrence is:
The longest common prefix of ["flower", "flow", "flight"] is:
questions.explanation: The three strings share the prefix 'fl' but 'flow' does not match 'flight' at position 2.

options: Only if the text is sorted
Only if the pattern is a substring
questions.explanation: The characters a, b, c appear in order in the text.

questions.text: For "leetcode", the index of the first non-repeating character is:
questions.explanation: 'l' appears exactly once, at index 0; every other character repeats.

questions.text: To verify that a multi-character ransom note can be formed from a magazine, the minimum required data structure is:
options: A frequency map (or array) of characters
questions.explanation: Duplicate letters in the note must consume magazine letters one-for-one, which requires counting frequencies.

questions.text: The minimum time complexity to determine if two length-n strings are anagrams (lowercase English alphabet):
options: O(n log n), by sorting both
O(n), by a single frequency count
questions.explanation: One pass builds the count, a second pass checks it; the alphabet size is constant.
